rv.q: "Turret" is another example, coming hard upon, of Chicago theater at its very best.
In turns, ominous, humorous and flat-out weird, “Turret” is a star turn for everyone involved.
“Turret” is that rare type of show that had me saying, “I love this” within 60 seconds of the curtain.
A Red Orchid Theatre's ambitious production, directed by the playwright at the Chopin Theatre, will blow you away.
Holloway has hit a nerve here while also sparking serious thoughts about what it is to be a man in dangerous times.
Turret is a thriller for the philosophical mind: it asks us how wild animals become domesticated and how domesticated animals become free.
When Green finally engages Rabbit, he begins asking his apparent protege/underling a series of questions that feel like part of a daily ritual: Did you dream?
Even though it's stagnant with an overly tangled and winding nature, I recommend Turret because it's well-produced, brazen and wonderfully acted.
I would recommend experiencing TURRET for yourself.
There are some potentially interesting ideas and motifs here, buried in a show that’s more intent on startling and overwhelming the audience than on communicating with it.
This is a stunning, futuristic, science fiction-esque story that will have you gripping at the edge of your seat from beginning to end.

cn.t: Critics hail this post-apocalyptic thriller as a riveting, Beckett-esque puzzle box showcasing Michael Shannon's intense performance, though a few find its ambiguity more frustrating than tantalizing.
